business: Headroom (UK software that finds revenue leakage for MSPs)
by_segment: Owner of a mid-sized UK MSP (11 to 30 staff, roughly £1m to £3m revenue)
Owner of a small UK MSP (5 to 10 staff, roughly £400k to £1m revenue)
Owner or commercial director of a larger UK MSP (31 to 50 staff, roughly £3m to £5m revenue)
by_behaviour: Already has a billing or BI tool
why_not: My PSA reporting and finance person already flag the agreements that lose money, and I go through it all at the QBRs. I might take the free audit out of curiosity, but I wouldn't pay £500 a month for something I think we mostly cover already.

Halo already tells me which agreements are underwater, and my service manager reviews it before renewals. I might take the free audit out of curiosity, but I'm not paying £240 a month for something my PSA and a decent quarterly review mostly cover.

I might take the free audit because I already know two clients are underpaying, but I do billing myself every month and I'm not paying £240 a month to a company with no customers, no reviews and no integrations to tell me what my spreadsheet mostly already does.

I'm not sending my clients' ticket data and contracts to a company I've never heard of, DPA or not. And I already pay for a reconciliation/BI tool that's meant to catch unbilled licences, so £240 a month on top looks like overlap.

Most of the 'unbilled' work it would find is stuff I do for free on purpose to keep long-standing clients happy, so a report telling me to go and charge for it isn't something I'd act on. Even with them doing the exports with me, it's still a call, a DPA and handing client contracts to a company I've never heard of, all to tell me something I already half know.

The freebies I do for clients are on purpose, it's how I've kept them for fifteen years. A report telling me I'm leaving money on the table doesn't change the fact that I'd have to go and have those awkward conversations myself, and I'm not going to put £240 a month behind something I'd mostly leave in a drawer.

I might take the free audit if it really is one call and an export, but I'm not paying £240 a month on spec. Our ticket categories are a mess, so I'd expect half the 'unbilled time' to be stuff we deliberately wrote off or miscoded, and I'd spend my evenings arguing with the report.

I'd probably take the free audit because I've got two clients I'm fairly sure are underpaying, but I'm not signing up to a monthly subscription off the back of a pitch. I've paid for a reporting tool before that nobody opened after setup, so I'll judge it on whether the audit report holds up when my service manager goes through it.
why_yes: The audit costs me nothing but 45 minutes and an export, and I watch margin per client anyway, so I'd book it to see the number. I'd only pay the £240 a month if the report shows billable money I actually believe I can collect without upsetting clients.

I've already got two clients I think are taking the mick, and a free audit with a DPA and UK hosting costs me 45 minutes, so I'll take it. Whether I pay £240 a month afterwards depends entirely on whether the number it finds is real money I'd actually bill, not goodwill I've chosen to give.
flip: If the free audit found a real recurring number, well beyond the subscription cost, that our own reporting had missed and that the clients actually accepted at renewal.

The free audit turning up a few clients I can actually see are over their agreement, with tickets I'd agree with, and more than the £2,880 after I've thrown out the noise. Or another UK MSP owner on r/msp saying it worked on messy PSA data.
Two or three owners in my peer group showing me their audit turned up well over the £2,880 in billable money they'd missed despite running Halo properly.

The free audit flagging my two suspect clients correctly, with tickets and contract clauses that my team checks and agrees with, and a total well above the £2,880 without us having to clean up our PSA first.
If the free audit actually found well over £2,880 a year I'd missed beyond those two clients, plus a couple of UK MSP owners I could ring who use it.

A peer MSP owner I trust telling me it found real leakage they'd genuinely missed, like licences we're paying for and never recharging, rather than goodwill work, and that raising it didn't cost them a client.

Several MSP owners I know of on r/msp or in the LinkedIn groups vouching for it, plus Cyber Essentials Plus or ISO 27001. Then I'd try the free audit to see whether it finds anything my current tool misses.
If the free audit turned up real billable money my current tool missed, and at least a few clients actually paid the uplift, I'd think about it.
A couple of MSPs my size I actually know, or someone in a peer group, telling me the audit found real money they billed and the clients didn't walk.
Another UK MSP owner I know and trust telling me they ran the audit, it found real money they actually billed, and it took under an hour of their time.

Proof from the audit that leakage keeps coming back every month, e.g. it finds new unbilled time and licence drift on clients we'd already sorted, plus it running off the PSA with no setup work from my team.
If the audit turned up real money I could bill, with the tickets behind it, and the monthly check dropped straight into my invoicing run without me logging into anything new, I'd pay.

If it only flagged hard, no-argument items like unbilled licences we're paying for ourselves and fed them straight into the next Autotask/Xero invoice, so there's no conversation to have, I might take the free audit and see.
If you pulled the data straight from my PSA yourselves with read-only access, with no export work on my side, and another small MSP owner I trust told me it found them real money.
If the free audit found well over £2,880 a year I genuinely accept, and a couple of MSP owners on r/msp I trust said it kept finding real money month after month, not just the first time.
Two or three owners in my peer group saying it found real money they actually billed without losing a client, with benchmark numbers to back it up.

If the free audit turned up a lot of clearly unbilled licences or contracted time, say £10k or more, that I could invoice without it feeling like a price rise, rather than goodwill work I'd have to argue about.
If the free audit turned up real unbilled licences or forgotten billable time, not goodwill, worth well over the £2,880, with the tickets to prove it, I'd consider the monthly check.
